Add lists a template in this host's templates.json, so any host can start
its agent here (agent template start <template> --host <this host>). The
agent is named after the template. --backend is what it runs (claude, agy,
aider or shell), --cwd the directory it runs in, and --brief the file it is
asked to read first (relative to --cwd, or to this directory); both must
exist. A template already listed under the name is refused: remove it
first. It edits this host's file only.

Usage:
  agent template add <template> [flags]

Examples:
  agent template add builder --backend claude --cwd /srv/project --brief docs/lanes/builder.md
  agent template add reviewer --backend claude --model claude-opus-5-5 --cwd /srv/project

Flags:
      --brief string   File the agent is asked to read first (relative to --cwd)
      --cwd string     Directory the agent runs in
  -h, --help           help for add
      --model string   Model the CLI runs on (default: its own default)

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)
